messages:
olivia (PM): Quick sync — I'm putting up a short PRD for a tiered routing + fallback playbook. Goal: predictable latency & cost across hosted/dedicated/private. Need agreement on MVP scope and launch criteria.

sam (SRE): Can you summarize the MVP? automatic variant mapping or manual table?

olivia (PM): MVP = routing policies per customer tier + region preference + a compatible-model fallback table. Automatic mapping optional for M1. Launch criteria focused on safety & observability.

dinesh (Infra): Important runtime note: region routing may require warm pools. If fallback routes cross regions, p95 latency will jump unless we pre-warm. Acceptance criteria should include p95 latency guardrails for fallback paths.

marie (ML Eval): Add correctness/regression checks: fallback correctness regression <= 1% on our eval prompt set, and per-route quality checks. Also need example prompts for each major workload.

kevin (Customer Success): Customers requested explicit model pinning and ability to opt out of automatic fallbacks (compliance use-cases). We should include an opt-out flag.

olivia (PM): Proposed launch checklist (MVP):
- support tiers: free / prod / enterprise (routing policy knobs)
- region preference list + region pinning opt-out
- compatible-variant table for common models (automatically consulted if enabled)
- telemetry: fallback_rate, latency_p50/p95, error_rate, correctness_regressions
- rollout plan: canary + automatic rollback on SLO breach

sam (SRE): Edge cases: what if a pinned model has no compatible fallback? options: fail request, queue, or route to a lowest-cost hosted model. Recommend failing by default unless customer allows fallback.

dinesh (Infra): Also add circuit-breakers: if fallback_rate > 10% for 5m OR error_rate > 5% then stop automatic fallback and alert. Add cost-threshold to avoid expensive cross-region fallbacks.

marie (ML Eval): Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- fallback correctness delta <= 1% on eval suite across 3 representative workloads
- end-to-end p95 for fallback route within 2x baseline p95 and < 500ms additional on average
- monitoring dash + alerts in Console before GA

olivia (PM): Draft config example I'll include in PRD:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  tiers: [free, prod, enterprise]
  region_preference: [us-west, us-east, eu-central]
  pinning_enabled: true
  compatible_variants:
    redwood-7b: [redwood-7b-q4, redwood-7b-int8]
    llama-2-13b: [llama-2-13b-q8]
  circuit_breaker:
    fallback_rate_threshold: 0.10
    window: 300 # seconds
```

sam (SRE): That YAML is helpful. I'll start a prototype mapping service and a small in-memory cache for variant lookups. ETA: 3 sprints for MVP plumbing.

kevin (Customer Success): +1 for opt-out and region pinning. I'll surface the PRD to two enterprise customers for early feedback.

deploy-bot: RFC draft created: https://redwood.internal/rfc/234-routing-playbook (status: draft)

olivia (PM): Action items: olivia update PRD with these ACs by Friday; sam prototype mapping; dinesh cost/warm-pool estimate; marie build eval prompts; kevin customer feedback. We'll reconvene next Tue to finalize scope.

marie (ML Eval): :thumbsup: Also adding a small regression harness to fail fast if fallback degrades quality significantly.

sam (SRE): One more question — should fallbacks prefer same-architecture variants where possible? e.g., quantized same-arch before switching to smaller arch. I think yes.

olivia (PM): Yes, prefer same-arch -> quantized -> smaller arch. I'll add to ordering rules.

kevin (Customer Success): FYI one customer asked for per-tenant custom fallback lists — may be an enterprise add-on.

olivia (PM): Noted. We'll scope as enterprise-only feature. Thanks all.
